NONE: › a floating object on the top of the sea, used for directing ships and warning them of possible danger

T: › [ T ] to prevent someone or something from sinking

T usually passive: › [ T usually passive ] to make someone feel happier or more confident about a situation
› [ T usually passive ] to support something and make it more successful

example: The very salty water buoyed her (up) as she swam.
她游泳時，含鹽量非常高的水使她漂浮了起來。
She was buoyed (up) by the warm reception her audience gave her.
觀眾們熱烈的歡迎使她倍受鼓舞。
House prices have been buoyed (up) in the area by the possibility of a new factory opening.
因為可能有一家新工廠在此開設，所以該地區的房價一直居高不下。

NONE: 歡欣鼓舞的；輕鬆愉快的

example: After reading the letter he was in a buoyant mood.
讀了信後，他高興得快要飄起來了。
房屋市場依然是有賺頭的。
